entries.title: QE - QUANTITATIVE EASING
entries.body:
An unconventional monetary policy in which a central bank buys financial assets on a large scale, mainly government bonds and asset-backed securities, in order to inject liquidity into the financial system. The goal is to lower long-term interest rates, stimulate credit and, ultimately, support economic activity when conventional tools (such as lowering the policy rate) have reached their limits, particularly when the rate is close to zero (*zero lower bound*).

QE was widely deployed by the major central banks starting with the financial crisis of 2008. The US Federal Reserve (Fed), the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Bank of Japan (BoJ) carried out successive programs that considerably inflated the size of their balance sheets. This monetary expansion is criticized for its redistributive effects: by driving up the price of financial assets (stocks, bonds, real estate), QE benefits the holders of these assets more than the real economy, which illustrates the Cantillon effect.

In the Bitcoin community, quantitative easing is often cited as one of the fundamental motivations for adopting BTC. Faced with a money creation perceived as unlimited and discretionary, Bitcoin offers a transparent and immutable monetary policy, with issuance capped at 21 million units.

entries.title: QR CODE
entries.body:
A type of two-dimensional barcode that can be quickly scanned by mobile devices. The QR code stores information as black and white pixels arranged in a square on a white background. An important characteristic of QR codes is that they embed Reed-Solomon error correction codes, which make it possible to restore the data even if the QR code is partially obscured.

The QR code is widely used on Bitcoin to facilitate the transmission of information between two devices. It is mainly used to share receiving addresses, encoded in URI format in accordance with BIP-0021. But its use also extends to extended keys, PSBTs, Lightning invoices, etc.

*QR code stands for "Quick Response Code".*

entries.title: QUBIT
entries.body: The basic unit of information on a quantum computer. These qubits can take the value 0, the value 1, or a superposition of 0 and 1. By using this superposition of states together with other quantum phenomena such as entanglement and quantum interference, a quantum computer can parallelize computational processes, and thus solve certain specific problems much faster.
